label: input token s at original positions 3-5
explanation: Fires only when the letter s is input during the original phase at position 3, 4 or 5. It never fires on s at positions 0-2 or 6+, on any other token, or on the delimiter, and it is essentially silent in the copy phase (2 tiny activations in the dev split). Within the window, firing is close to deterministic: dev precision 1.0 and recall 1.0. Magnitude is highest at position 4, which takes about 49% of the activation mass from about 33% of the firings; top examples are s at t=4 at about 1.0 of max, while s at t=3 or t=5 is often about 0.35-0.55. Magnitude does not depend on the previous token or the first token.

issues: None of the claims could be refuted. On the test split the predicate scores precision 1.0, recall 0.99998, F1 0.99999 and mass recall 0.999995.
Test misses: there is 1 missed activation (s at copy step 4 in an L=3 sequence, about 0.10 of max, 0% of mass) and 0 false positives. This is scattered noise, not a pattern.

The dev profile matches every claim. The feature fires only on in_tok s, never at t 0-2 or 6+, and never on the delimiter. The copy phase has 2 firings out of 41046. Mass shares by position are t=3 0.30, t=4 0.49 and t=5 0.21, so position 4 is the peak as claimed.
Firing on s at t=4 alone has precision 1.0, recall 0.34 and mass recall 0.50, which confirms that position 4 dominates the magnitude.

Small note: the profile shows a 0.207 firing rate when in_tok is s, which matches s at positions 3-5 out of all s inputs. Since recall is 1.0 inside the window, the window is complete. I did not directly test the claim that magnitude is independent of the previous token or first token, because the scoring tools only measure firing.
